## Data

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/), Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data were collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station LTER program, and packaged for Python by Horst, Hill and Gorman (2020). It is released under a CC0 licence.

This post asks the question: do the three penguin species in palmerspenguins differ in average body mass?

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
```

## Cleaning the data

Some penguins are missing a body mass measurement, so I drop those rows, and see how many remain.

```{python}
penguins = load_penguins()
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"])

len(penguins_clean)
```

## Summary table

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Body mass by species."

summary_table = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species", observed=True)["body_mass_g"]
    .agg(n="count", mean_mass_g="mean", sd_mass_g="std")
    .round(1)
)

summary_table
```

@tbl-summary shows that Gentoo penguins have the highest mean body mass, at `{python} summary_table.loc["Gentoo", "mean_mass_g"]` g.

## Figure

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body mass of penguins by species."

penguins_clean.boxplot(column="body_mass_g", by="species", grid=False)
plt.suptitle("")
plt.title("")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.show()
```

## What I found

@fig-penguin-mass agrees with the table. Gentoo penguins are clearly heavier than the other two species, while Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar body masses.
